newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle markets remain quiet - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle markets remain quiet - private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained quiet throughout the day Tuesday, after feedlot managers passed the few $70.00 per cwt bids offered this morning, feedlot sources said.

Some managers expressed optimism buyer interest would improve Wednesday, largely because of the lack of activity Monday and Tuesday. Many of last week's cattle sales have been shipped and packers were expected to begin securing next week's slaughter needs.
Higher beef prices at midday Tuesday failed to inspire packer bidding nor did it prompt feedlots to raise prices.
Asking prices remained at $72.00 to $73.00, with several managers confirming that $72.00 bid would prompt selling.

USDA reported beef cutout values closed up 2.00 to 2.14 cents per lb for choice cuts and up $0.69 to $0.78 for select cuts. Cutout values for choice 1-3 700-850 lb carcasses were quoted at 118.89 cents per lb, which USDA said is the highest level since June 1993.
